event.title: Chennai northeast monsoon · Oct–Nov 2026
event.subtitle: Chennai · Tiruvallur · Kancheepuram · Chengalpattu
event.context: Chennai gets most of its rain from the northeast monsoon (Oct–Dec). Heavy rain from 17 Oct 2026 brought flash-flood warnings (The Week, 18 Oct 2026); on 2 Nov the city averaged 76 mm in 24 h (NewsBytes). IMD/IANS flagged a Bay of Bengal system that could bring more heavy rain around 15–20 Nov. Then vs now: during Cyclone Michaung (3–8 Dec 2023) no Sentinel-1 radar pass covered central Chennai between 30 Nov and 25 Dec 2023 (ASF archive search), so free radar missed the city's worst recent flood; ISRO mapped it with RISAT-1A on 7 Dec. In 2026 NISAR images the whole city on two tracks (149, 156) on back-to-back days every 12 days, and the western suburbs on a third (84).
event.caveat: Most of Chennai is dense city, where street flooding is hard to see with radar backscatter alone; the map is most reliable over open land, lake beds, marshes (Pallikaranai) and river floodplains. Many tanks fill every monsoon: water that is new since the dry season is shown as flood even where it is seasonal.

validation.protocol: Model trained in Assam plus ONE automatically labelled Chennai dry-season scene (14 Jul, T84), fixed before any Chennai result was seen; scored on northeast-monsoon passes it never saw, including the other track (T156). Reference: Sentinel-2 cloud-free open water within a day; open sea excluded. Dry-season dates (small tanks) score IoU 0.13-0.25 for every method.

model.name: JalDrishti hybrid
model.learner: LightGBM gradient-boosted trees (binary: open water vs not)

features.name: hh_minus_hv
features.description: HH − HV (dB): polarisation ratio; separates smooth water, vegetation and urban scattering

features.name: hh_rel_p10
features.description: HH backscatter relative to the scene's darkest 10% (dB): how water-like, scene-normalised

features.name: hh_rel_p50
features.description: HH backscatter relative to the scene median (dB): dark compared with this scene's typical land

features.name: hv_rel_p50
features.description: HV cross-pol backscatter relative to the scene median (dB): vegetation volume vs smooth water

features.name: d_hh
features.description: HH change from the pre-flood reference median (dB): strong drop = new open water

features.name: d_hv
features.description: HV change from the pre-flood reference median (dB)

features.name: hh_s7
features.description: HH texture: standard deviation in a 7×7 window (water is smooth, land is rough)

features.name: d_hh_m7
features.description: HH change averaged over 7×7 pixels (140 m): spatially coherent change, not speckle

features.name: d_hh_m15
features.description: HH change averaged over 15×15 pixels (300 m): neighbourhood context

features.name: hand
features.description: Height Above Nearest Drainage (m), ASF GLO-30 HAND: low ground floods first

features.name: jrc
features.description: JRC Global Surface Water occurrence 1984–2021 (%): how often this place was water historically

model.rule: flood water = P(water now) > 0.5, OR (HH < −15 dB and HAND < 10 m) as a physics rescue (rescued pixels get p ≥ 0.51); new flood = water now × (1 − water in the pre-flood reference passes), outside JRC permanent water
model.veg_rule: flooded vegetation = HH rises > 3σ above no-change and more than HV, HV stable, under trees/grass/wetland (not cropland)
model.physics_terms: Per-pixel log-odds from the scene-adaptive water/land Gaussian mixture (water-like now, dry before) and terrain priors (HAND bands after Nobre et al. 2011, slope); shown in the pixel panel.

rainfall.source: ERA5 reanalysis (Copernicus/ECMWF) via Open-Meteo archive, mean of a 3×3 point grid over the area
rainfall.note: NASA GPM IMERG will replace this once the GES DISC archive is authorised for the project's Earthdata account

tracker.label: Modelled
tracker.method: Cross-track linear interpolation: each pixel blends the nearest earlier and later NISAR passes (any track) by time.

validation.protocol: Each NISAR pass hidden in turn and predicted from the other passes (any track); scored against that pass's own map (confident flood vs dry, 200 m cells). Assam and Thailand.

tracker.note: Estimate between passes from the passes before and after. Not an observation.
